threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it 'Stokey' instead of Stoke Newington—locals know it's an unwritten rule to use the full name when you're proper.
Caught a night bus from Brixton to Clapham, and a guy serenaded us with an old soul song. Only in South London would strangers nod along like it’s a concert.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: It hit me when I saw a dance party break out in the middle of the street at Sonnenallee. No one cared about the noise, just pure joy.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you catch a Späti open at 3 AM serving fresh currywurst while a group of artists debates philosophy on the sidewalk.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local when they sidestep the dog crap on the sidewalk without even looking up, while newcomers are too busy staring at their phones.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a glimpse of a street performer directing traffic today near the Civic Center. Just another day of chaos in Muni-land, but the rhythm was oddly comforting.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia's plazas are just for selfies, but locals really gather there for spontaneous concerts and community events, especially on weekends.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their confusion over paella vs. fideuà—locals know you don’t mix the two for Sunday family lunch.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it 'the tube' instead of 'the underground' and look puzzled at the bus stops. Classic newbie move.
Last night on the 59, a couple tried to argue their way out of a £50 fine for not tapping in. They insisted the driver had winked at them first.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The day I saw a group of kids roller-skating past a kebab stand blaring Beethoven, I knew this place had a pulse of its own.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain do you find spontaneous punk shows in abandoned buildings, blending gritty charm with a wild energy you won't find anywhere else.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s a local when they can spot a tourist just looking at the BART map, but barely grimace at another Muni delay from a dog on the tracks.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a rider serenading passengers with a ukulele at Civic Center despite the delays. Only in SF do breakdowns spark live music.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think 'Gràcia' is just for the parks and plazas; they miss the old factories turned into art studios, full of local character.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell by their confusion at the lack of straws in cafes—still ordering drinks the 'old' way, missing the local tapas hustle.
